page: Microsoft Azure D32nls_v6 is a network-optimized, low-memory virtual machine belonging to the Dnlv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, though it is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong performance in memory bandwidth and specific computational tasks. The server achieves a strong rating in large-block read-only memory bandwidth at 202.93 GB/sec, alongside strong Geekbench single-core (2079.0) and multi-core (16529.0) scores. It excels in text generation for small LLM models, reaching a top-tier speed of 385.75 tokens/sec, and shows strong prompt processing capabilities. However, write bandwidth for large blocks remains average at 87.93 GB/sec, and multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng falls within the average range at 26575.61.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D32nls_v6 offers high compute density and advanced instruction support without the added cost of bundled local storage or high memory allocations. This makes it a resource-efficient choice for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. The server is well-suited for network-intensive applications, static web serving, software compilation, and lightweight machine learning inference tasks utilizing its AMX and AVX-512 capabilities.
